cells.tense: You are reading the pattern of a connection in this room and choosing it with your eyes open.
cells.ask: Tell one person the thing you noticed about how the two of you work, in your own words, without asking them to agree with it.
cells.core:
Pattern-reading is live in you right now and it's steering. You catch how two people actually shift when nobody's posing — not the story about what it means, the movement itself — and you let that read choose your next step. When you say why you're in it, the person across from you hears the choice as real, and the bond sits on firmer ground.

What lags is the speech. You keep the read to yourself and let the connection ride on assumption. The same clear eye that shows you how it works is what asks you to say it out loud. Say it plainly and let their response be its own thing. Saying it is how the pick gets made.
cells.sheetLine: You can see how the two of you work, and you're choosing it.
cells.verb: choosing a meeting of two streams into one flow
cells.place: held in the shape something makes when its surface is lifted off

cells.tense: You are already living in a version of this connection that hasn't happened yet, bracing for how it must go.
cells.ask: Name one pattern you've started explaining about the two of you and leave the sentence unfinished, out loud, without filling it in.
cells.core:
Read clean, and reading a connection follows from what's already happened between you. You catch how it moves, what you catch feeds the next step, and dreaming forward grows out of ground you've actually walked — vision that arrives after the experience, not before it. That is the face this carries when it's whole.

Lately the read runs ahead of the ground. A look gets fitted to where it's heading, a silence checked against a future only you can picture, and the fit tightens when nothing settles. Forecasting has become the relationship. The pull back is to let one thing be what it actually is today, not what it might turn into.

cells.tense: You saw the pattern clearly once, and you have been standing behind that moment ever since.
cells.ask: Put one thing you notice about how something works into a sentence a friend could repeat back to you, and say it without softening it.
cells.core:
At full stretch this arrives without argument. You catch how something holds together, you say it, and it lands — no need for agreement to keep going. That ease is what the card carries when it's whole: a read that comes, gets spoken, and settles.

Standing where you are now, the read that once landed isn't coming out again. Connections that call for a decision keep arriving and stay at the edge. The eye isn't broken. What went quiet is the trust that what you see is worth putting into words. Pick something small you understand and say it plainly.
cells.sheetLine: You can still see it. You've stopped saying what you see.

cells.tense: You are already reading how the two of you work and calling it something that just happened.
cells.ask: Say out loud, to one person, 'I chose this' about a connection you've been describing as something that happened to you.
cells.core:
When it's owned, seeing how a connection works and picking it feel like one motion. You catch the shape, you move with it, and you name it as yours — which makes the bond steadier, not smaller. Pattern read, choice made, both said out loud.

Here the read runs and the saying doesn't. You saw which way something was going and moved with it, and the story since has been that things turned out that way on their own. Nothing's hidden. The read is just going unattributed, and the one who did it is standing right here. Say it once.
cells.sheetLine: You're already picking this. You just haven't owned it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that this person's vision is flowing or blocked in a relationship or calling — the record only gives a capacity of seeing pattern and choosing connection, not their history. A reader could say 'that's not what's happening, I just don't have anyone to do this with.' The ask survives being wrong because it's a concrete act of saying a pattern in your own words to someone who's shown interest — useful even if the read about a specific connection is off. The sentence that serves the writer is 'you're the one deciding what gets passed on' — it flatters the reader with authorship they may not be exercising yet; I'm cutting it toward what they actually do.
